declared_versus_inferred_temperature.text:
{
  "entry_id": "declared_versus_inferred_temperature",
  "schema_version": "0.1",
  "kind": "claim",
  "claim": "Temperature enters the two sides differently, and the difference is not symmetric. In the simulation the thermostat realises the declared value, so citing a temperature there records WHY the number was chosen and is not evidence about the model's temperature -- the model's temperature is what was declared. In the experiment nothing actuates the sample and the only thermometer reads the room, so a temperature used there is INFERRED, and citing the same entry is a claim about the sample. The uncertainty therefore sits entirely on the experiment side.",
  "subject": [
    { "kind": "quantity", "id": "temperature" },
    { "kind": "observable", "id": "tracer_diffusivity" }
  ],
  "source": "computed:temperature_asymmetry",
  "grade": "E4",
  "grade_tag": "computed",
  "source_ref": "src_store_derivation",
  "validity_conditions": "Holds while both halves hold, and each is separately falsifiable. The experiment half rests on sample_temperature_not_actuated and on lab_ambient_temperature being a reading of the room: connect the temperature stage, or record where the thermometer sits relative to the sample, and it changes. The simulation half rests on the engine's thermostat realising its setpoint, which is a property of that engine and is NOT held in this store -- it is named here as an input rather than asserted as knowledge, and a simulation seat is the one that can confirm or refute it. E4 rather than E3 because a consequence is never better than the derivation that produced it, whatever the grade of its inputs. What this entry does NOT say is how large the experiment-side uncertainty is; that needs the thermometer's distance from the sample and how well the two track, and neither is known.",
  "date": "2026-09-19",
  "supersedes": null,
  "conflict_with": [],
  "curated_by": "kyuhwan"
}

lab_ambient_temperature.text:
{
  "entry_id": "lab_ambient_temperature",
  "schema_version": "0.1",
  "kind": "claim",
  "claim": "The laboratory's ambient temperature is 20 degrees Celsius, read off a thermometer by the operator. It is a reading and not a setpoint, and it is the room's rather than the sample's -- which is what makes it an operator reading at E3 and not a calibration at E2.",
  "numbers": [
    {
      "name": "ambient_temperature",
      "value": 293,
      "unit": "K",
      "source": "operator_read:kyuhwan_20260917",
      "grade": "E3",
      "precision": "significant_figures",
      "note": "the reading was reported as 20 degrees Celsius. The store carries kelvin because the unit registry is multiplicative -- si_factor and a dimension vector cannot express an offset unit, so Celsius cannot enter it at all. 293 K rather than 293.15 K: the exact conversion would claim five figures from a reading given to the nearest degree, and the 0.15 K it drops is far inside the resolution of the reading."
    }
  ],
  "validity_conditions": "The room as of 2026-09-17, operator read off a thermometer. CORRECTED 2026-09-19: this entry used to reason that the value could not be a setpoint because nothing actuates the temperature. That premise was false and the conclusion was right. The room IS held, by continuous air conditioning; what is not actuated is the SAMPLE, and the entry had collapsed the two. The grade never rested on that argument: 20 C is a value someone READ, which 12 grades differently from a setpoint, and a room value applied to the sample is not a measurement of the sample. A right answer standing on a wrong reason is the thing that rots, and as written the sentence asserted that this room is uncontrolled. The controlled room does not shrink the sample question, it ISOLATES it: with the room held, whatever still moves at the sample is local -- illumination, a contacting objective, the stage -- and those have their own open gap. Do not read 'the room is controlled' as 'temperature is handled'. WHERE the thermometer sits is now stated rather than inferred (no_thermometer_at_the_sample): it reads the room, and how far that is from the sample and how well the two track are both unknown. A plan needing the viscosity or the thermal energy AT THE SAMPLE stands on that gap rather than on this entry. Water's viscosity moves by roughly two percent per kelvin, so in explore mode a drift of about a kelvin does not move a decade and can be ignored, while in confirm mode it cannot. The date the reading was taken is not recorded either -- what is dated 2026-09-17 is the operator's statement that it is a reading.",
  "source": "operator_read:kyuhwan_20260917",
  "grade_tag": "operator_read",
  "subject": [
    {
      "kind": "quantity",
      "id": "ambient_temperature"
    },
    {
      "kind": "quantity",
      "id": "temperature"
    }
  ],
  "grade": "E3",
  "source_ref": "src_operator_read_20260917",
  "date": "2026-09-17",
  "supersedes": null,
  "conflict_with": [],
  "curated_by": "kyuhwan"
}

room_temperature_is_controlled.text:
{
  "entry_id": "room_temperature_is_controlled",
  "schema_version": "0.1",
  "kind": "claim",
  "claim": "The room is held continuously by air conditioning. There is a setpoint on this instrument's environment -- it is the room's, not the sample's.",
  "subject": [
    { "kind": "quantity", "id": "temperature" },
    { "kind": "quantity", "id": "ambient_temperature" }
  ],
  "source": "operator_read:kyuhwan_20260919",
  "grade": "E3",
  "grade_tag": "operator_read",
  "source_ref": "src_operator_read_20260919",
  "validity_conditions": "This laboratory as of 2026-09-19, read by the operator. It runs opposite to how it sounds, and that is the reason it is worth an entry: holding the room does not shrink the sample question, it ISOLATES it. With the room held, whatever still moves at the sample is local -- illumination, a contacting objective, the stage, the trapping laser -- and each of those has its own gap. Do not read 'the room is controlled' as 'temperature is handled'. It also corrected a sentence in this store: lab_ambient_temperature argued that 20 C could not be a setpoint because nothing actuates the temperature, which collapsed 'nothing actuates the SAMPLE' into 'nothing actuates'. That grade never rested on the argument and did not move; the reasoning did. What this entry does NOT say: what the setpoint is, how tightly the room holds it, and how well the sample follows the room. The third is the one that matters and all three are open -- a controlled room is not a controlled sample, and the distance between them is still unmeasured.",

trap_heating_detection_bound.text:
{
  "entry_id": "trap_heating_detection_bound",
  "schema_version": "0.1",
  "kind": "claim",
  "claim": "The operator recalls not noticing a temperature change in the sample unless the infrared trapping laser was driven above roughly 20 percent on its dial. This records where noticing stopped, by means that were not recorded.",
  "subject": [
    { "kind": "device", "id": "optical_tweezers" },
    { "kind": "configuration", "id": "trapping" },
    { "kind": "quantity", "id": "temperature" }
  ],
  "source": "operator_recall:kyuhwan_20260919",
  "grade": "E5",
  "grade_tag": "operator_recall",
  "source_ref": "src_operator_recall_20260919",
  "validity_conditions": "THIS IS NOT A LIMIT AND MAY NOT BE USED AS ONE. 'Keep it under 20 percent' is the sentence someone lifts out of an entry and uses to parameterise a laser, and three separate rules forbid that: safety limits live in a file a person writes and in deterministic code (P0, 2.1 rule 7), they do not transfer (10.3 rule 4), and the grade forbids it on its own -- an E5 may not parameterise an irreversible action without a person's individual approval, and raising laser power onto a sample is irreversible to the sample. Anyone needing a bound writes one in envelope/safety.json after confirming it physically. Three things this says less than it appears to. It is RECALLED, not read, which is why it is E5 while the neighbouring instrument facts are E3. It is a DETECTION BOUND and not a zero: 'did not notice' was measured by unrecorded means, and 'no heating below 20 percent' is a stronger claim than was made. And 20 PERCENT IS A DIAL READING, not a power: a percentage of an unstated maximum is not a quantity, and writing it into numbers[] would not make it one -- the same ruling that keeps a nominal magnification out of numbers[], wearing different clothes. It does not close the heating gap. A measured heating rate is still absent, and a gap that looks satisfied by an E5 recollection is a false absence running backwards. What it does is sharpen what to measure: sweep the dial with a thermometer that has a recorded position, and the bound becomes a curve.",
  "date": "2026-09-19",
  "supersedes": null,
  "conflict_with": [],
  "curated_by": "kyuhwan"
}

Slot: A7, which owns the driving term, with the orchestrator second. trapping_laser_identity.text:
{
  "entry_id": "trapping_laser_identity",
  "schema_version": "0.1",
  "kind": "claim",
  "claim": "The trapping laser emits at 1064 nm and is rated to a maximum of 5 W measured AT THE GENERATOR. The model is an Aresis Tweez 300.",
  "numbers": [
    {
      "name": "wavelength",
      "value": 1064,
      "unit": "nm",
      "source": "operator_read:kyuhwan_20260919",
      "grade": "E3",
      "precision": "significant_figures"
    },
    {
      "name": "rated_max_power",
      "value": 5,
      "unit": "W",
      "source": "operator_read:kyuhwan_20260919",
      "grade": "E3",
      "precision": "significant_figures",
      "note": "at the generator, which `at` now names as a resolvable id rather than leaving it to prose. Not at the sample, and not at any point after it",
      "at": "optical_tweezers"
    }
  ],
  "subject": [
    {
      "kind": "device",
      "id": "optical_tweezers"
    },
    {
      "kind": "configuration",
      "id": "trapping"
    }
  ],
  "source": "operator_read:kyuhwan_20260919",
  "grade": "E3",
  "grade_tag": "operator_read",
  "source_ref": "src_operator_read_20260919",
  "validity_conditions": "AT THE GENERATOR. Written without a place, 'the laser is 5 W' is false at every point the beam actually reaches: between the generator and the sample sit losses nothing here records and the objective's transmission at 1064 nm, which is itself an open gap. The power a sample sees is a separate fact and it is absent (gap trap_power_at_the_sample). A RATED MAXIMUM IS NOT A PERMISSION. 5 W is what the device can emit, not what this laboratory allows; what it allows is written by a person in envelope/safety.json, and that file does not exist. 10.2 gates transferred spec values on exactly that file, with the reason that a spec number not placed beside limit values gets used as a limit -- the gate applies to transfers and so does not block this entry, which came from the operator, but the hazard it names does not care where the number came from. NOT MACHINE-READABLE, and that is a limit of the schema rather than of this entry: `validity` carries quantity-to-interval pairs, so 'at the generator' has nowhere to go and a query cannot act on it. This is the second such case -- the first being that lab_ambient_temperature is a reading of the room and not of the sample -- and both are raised with manager-librarian. The model name arrived after the numbers and the sequence is worth keeping: asked for it, the operator said there was none, and Aresis Tweez 300 was confirmed later the same day. The numbers are still the operator's own reading and their grade does not move -- spec: and operator_read: are both E3 -- so what the model adds is a handle, `model` being addressable, and not authority. `at` on the power carries the place now; the wavelength has none, which is why the field sits on the number and not on this entry.",

  "supersedes": null,
  "conflict_with": [],
  "curated_by": "kyuhwan",
  "identifiers": {
    "model": "Aresis Tweez 300"
  }
}

{
  "entry_id": "tweez300_reports_nothing_back",
  "schema_version": "0.1",
  "kind": "claim",
  "claim": "The Tweez 300's TCP interface has no readback of any kind -- no position, no force, no trap list, no calibration -- and a return code of 0 means the GUI accepted the command, not that anything happened. Six distinct ways a command can be ignored all return 0: a breakpoint whose enable bits are unset, release bits that do not cover the value, repeat left disabled, a pattern that overruns the calibrated range and is silently clipped to the edge, a GUI calibrated at a different objective so every commanded micrometre is wrong by that ratio, and a named trap that holds no bead.",
  "subject": [
    {
      "kind": "device",
      "id": "optical_tweezers"
    },
    {
      "kind": "configuration",
      "id": "trapping"
    }
  ],
  "source": "prior_run:agentic-microscope@safety-2026-09-03",
  "grade": "E3",
  "source_ref": "src_prior_safety_memo",
  "validity_conditions": "Ruled TRANSFER under 10.2.1 and passed 10.3 rule 1, so it caps at E3 -- a run taken in another project is not a run taken here. 10.2's hardware-control-path row is open and says in its own rule that it does not wait for envelope/, because wrapping a control path needs no safety limit. Slot: A4, which screens on automatable and read_back, with O1 preflight as the second consumer -- a preflight that reads back to confirm has nothing to read here. This is what read_back: false means on that row, stated rather than left as a flag. Confirmation has to come from outside the interface: by eye in the GUI, or by measuring the result in camera data. Note the contrast with the piezo, which range-checks a trajectory against the travel its controller reports and REFUSES rather than clipping -- two devices on one instrument, opposite behaviours at the same boundary, and only one of them tells you.",
  "date": "2026-09-19",
  "supersedes": null,

The source document's own open-questions list still says this direction is unmeasured and calls it the most consequential gap in the document; the body of the same document records the measurement two days later. The list is stale, not the measurement -- see the pfs_offset_sign_unmeasured gap for the direction that really is still open.",
